verdict.rationale: Snyk documents multiple AI-driven remediation paths — the Remediation Agent (LLM-driven, generates and applies fix plans), `snyk fix --agentic`, `/snyk-fix`/`/snyk-batch-fix` slash commands, DeepCode AI autofixes, and PR-based fix workflows for Snyk Open Source (snyk-docs-12, snyk-docs-13, snyk-docs-21, snyk-docs-23, snyk-docs-29, snyk-docs-30). However, hands-on community reports specifically fault Snyk's PR remediation output — creating 'dozens or hundreds of PRs to update dependencies rather than rewriting them,' missing version bumps, and incorrectly replacing legitimately-forked packages (snyk-comm-2, snyk-comm-7) — a concrete contradiction of the review-and-merge PR quality implied by the story. Missing for 10: independent verification that the newer agentic Remediation Agent (vs. older dependency-bump PRs) produces high-quality review-ready PRs, and resolution of the documented PR-quality complaints.
